title: The Space-Time Membrane Model: Unifying Quantum Mechanics and General Relativity through Elastic Membrane Dynamics
content: We present the Space-Time Membrane (STM) model, treating our four-dimensional spacetime as an elastic membrane with a mirror universe on its opposite side. Energy external to the membrane deforms it, creating gravitational curvature akin to mass–energy distributions in General Relativity, while uniform energy within the membrane remains curvature-neutral. Particles emerge as oscillatory membrane excitations, partnered with mirror antiparticles on the far side. A modified elastic wave equation, featuring tension, bending stiffness, and space-time-dependent variations in membrane stiffness, reproduces key elements of General Relativity and aligns with Quantum Field Theory. Metric perturbations mirror the structure of the Einstein Field Equations, yielding phenomena such as time dilation, gravitational effects, and non-singular black hole interiors. Stable standing waves and controlled stiffness variations also produce interference patterns and entanglement analogues, echoing quantum experiments within a deterministic framework. Interpreting photons as wave + anti-wave oscillations ensures masslessness, correct polarisations, U(1) gauge symmetry, and Lorentz invariance. High-energy processes involving photons and matter–antimatter pairs remain consistent with this view. Adjusting an intrinsic coupling constant aligns time-averaged stiffness changes with observed vacuum energy, explaining the cosmological constant. Hence, the STM model offers a geometric, deterministic approach bridging quantum phenomena and large-scale curvature without modifying QFT.
